findings.text: Allocation helper chooses between a device supplied map allocator when present and the generic coherent allocator otherwise, forwarding size handle and flags and returning the resulting area.

Address accessors expose device visible locations for descriptor storage and for driver and device event areas, selecting packed stored addresses or split base plus intra queue offsets according to layout.

Split ring layout places descriptors at the supplied base, availability array immediately after them, and used array after availability with alignment rounding, while total footprint accounts for descriptors plus availability and used headers and per entry state with the same alignment.

Creation of split and packed queues records name index callback device notifier mapping and barrier preference, clears reset and ownership, derives indirect event and layout from negotiated features and context, forces strong barriers under platform ordering, and starts in broken state only under hardened notification builds.
Common initialization sets free count to queue size, clears consumed markers and added count and event flag, and for packed layout sets the wrap related event bit in the last used index.

When no completion callback is supplied the driver shadows a no interrupt or disable indication and publishes it to the peer visible availability or driver event flags, with split event index mode keeping the change shadow only.
Per descriptor bookkeeping allocates zeroed state and extra arrays sized by queue depth and links extras into a single chain in index order with the final entry returning to the start.

In order mode is defined by either split or packed in order layout and changes attachment so packed in order relies on next available position and skips the free head while other modes start the free head at zero and other paths reset the batch marker to its maximum value.
Queue memory allocation prefers the map API path when the device advertises it and otherwise uses exact page allocation with page alignment, returning null on allocation failure.
Insertion of a newly created queue into the device queue list is serialized by the device queue list lock held only across list linkage.

Split state keeps descriptor availability and used pointers plus count queue address and shadow flags and index with free head and batch marker, while packed state keeps descriptor and two single entry event pointers plus counts addresses sizes wrap counters shadow flags and availability markers.

Packed creation allocates descriptor storage then driver event then device event with zeroed memory, frees all already allocated parts on any failure, forwards to inner creation, releases everything if inner creation fails, and on success marks the queue as owning its ring.

Split creation aborts and releases the queue object if state allocation fails, otherwise proceeds through ring initialization common initialization attachment and list insertion without further failure paths shown.

Platform probe allocates device state, maps the control region, validates identity and version, rejects placeholder identifiers, programs page size and addressability, registers the virtio device and releases state through the device release hook, while removal unregisters the device.

Queue discovery acquires the single platform interrupt as shared, optionally enables it for system wake, skips unnamed entries and sets up remaining queues in order with teardown on error, supported by a config table covering accessors status reset queue management features bus naming shared memory and callback synchronization.
Power handling delegates suspend and resume to generic virtio device helpers, reprogramming the guest page size on resume for legacy version, exposed through system sleep operations.

Command line instantiation parses size base interrupt and optional identifier, rejects malformed text or zero interrupt, creates memory and interrupt resources, lazily registers a root parent, instantiates platform devices with incrementing identifiers, reports existing entries on read, and can unregister all children and the parent where supported.
Exact page allocation without map API derives the device address from the CPU physical address and treats any narrowing as a one time warning with release of the pages and failure return.
Descriptor and event address queries require that the queue owns its ring storage and abort if that precondition does not hold.

MMIO identity expects a four character little endian signature spelling virt, supports versions one through three inclusive, and treats device identifier zero as a nonfunctional placeholder that ends probing without error beyond nodev.

Shared memory selection uses an identifier register followed by low and high halves for length and address, with all one bits length meaning no region, while device discovery uses compatibility virtio,mmio and ACPI identifier LNRO0005.

Split ring footprint and placement derive from descriptor count and alignment with descriptors first then availability then aligned used area including fixed headers for flags index and event fields plus per entry used elements.
